claim: Models of cell function that assign a variable to each gene frequently lead to systems of equations with many parameters whose behavior is obscure.
source: Models of cell function that assign a variable to each gene frequently lead to systems of equations with many parameters whose behavior is obscure.
evidence: This is a statement made in the abstract about the limitations of gene-based models.

claim: Geometric models reduce dynamics to intuitive pictorial elements that provide compact representations for sparse in vivo data and transparent descriptions of developmental transitions.
source: Geometric models reduce dynamics to intuitive pictorial elements that provide compact representations for sparse in vivo data and transparent descriptions of developmental transitions.
evidence: This is a claim about the advantages of geometric models stated in the abstract.

claim: A geometric model fit to vulval development in Caenorhabditis elegans implies a phase diagram where cell-fate choices are displayed in a plane defined by EGF and Notch signaling levels.
source: To illustrate, a geometric model fit to vulval development in Caenorhabditis elegans, implies a phase diagram where cell-fate choices are displayed in a plane defined by EGF and Notch signaling levels.
evidence: This claim describes the main result of the model presented in the paper.

claim: The phase diagram defines allowable and forbidden cell-fate transitions as EGF or Notch levels change.
source: This diagram defines allowable and forbidden cell-fate transitions as EGF or Notch levels change, and explains surprising observations previously attributed to context-dependent action of these signals.
evidence: This is a claim about what the phase diagram reveals, supported by the model results.

claim: The phase diagram explains surprising observations previously attributed to context-dependent action of EGF and Notch signals.
source: This diagram defines allowable and forbidden cell-fate transitions as EGF or Notch levels change, and explains surprising observations previously attributed to context-dependent action of these signals.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model's ability to explain experimental observations without invoking context-dependent signaling.

claim: The phase diagram reveals the existence of special points at which minor changes in signal levels lead to strong epistatic interactions between EGF and Notch.
source: The diagram also reveals the existence of special points at which minor changes in signal levels lead to strong epistatic interactions between EGF and Notch.
evidence: This claim is supported by the identification of triple points in the phase diagram.

claim: The model correctly predicts experiments near special points in the phase diagram.
source: Our model correctly predicts experiments near these points and suggests specific timed perturbations in signals that can lead to additional unexpected outcomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of model predictions with experimental data from Barkoulas et al., 2013.

claim: The model suggests specific timed perturbations in signals that can lead to additional unexpected outcomes.
source: Our model correctly predicts experiments near these points and suggests specific timed perturbations in signals that can lead to additional unexpected outcomes.
evidence: This is a predictive claim based on model simulations shown in Figure 6.

claim: Six vulval precursor cells (VPCs), P3.p-P8.p, are developmentally equivalent in C. elegans.
source: Here, six vulval precursor cells (VPCs), P3.p-P8.p, which are developmentally equivalent (P3.p is less competent and ignored in the model), receive an EGF signal from the anchor cell (AC), and interact through Notch signaling, to eventually assume one of three different terminal fates (Sternberg and Horvitz, 1989).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans vulval development, supported by citation.

claim: P3.p is less competent than other VPCs and is ignored in the model.
source: Here, six vulval precursor cells (VPCs), P3.p-P8.p, which are developmentally equivalent (P3.p is less competent and ignored in the model), receive an EGF signal from the anchor cell (AC), and interact through Notch signaling, to eventually assume one of three different terminal fates (Sternberg and Horvitz, 1989).
evidence: This is a modeling assumption based on known biological differences.

claim: VPCs receive an EGF signal from the anchor cell (AC).
source: Here, six vulval precursor cells (VPCs), P3.p-P8.p, which are developmentally equivalent (P3.p is less competent and ignored in the model), receive an EGF signal from the anchor cell (AC), and interact through Notch signaling, to eventually assume one of three different terminal fates (Sternberg and Horvitz, 1989).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans vulval development, supported by citation.

claim: VPCs interact through Notch signaling.
source: Here, six vulval precursor cells (VPCs), P3.p-P8.p, which are developmentally equivalent (P3.p is less competent and ignored in the model), receive an EGF signal from the anchor cell (AC), and interact through Notch signaling, to eventually assume one of three different terminal fates (Sternberg and Horvitz, 1989).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans vulval development, supported by citation.

claim: VPCs eventually assume one of three different terminal fates.
source: Here, six vulval precursor cells (VPCs), P3.p-P8.p, which are developmentally equivalent (P3.p is less competent and ignored in the model), receive an EGF signal from the anchor cell (AC), and interact through Notch signaling, to eventually assume one of three different terminal fates (Sternberg and Horvitz, 1989).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans vulval development, supported by citation.

claim: Cells P6.p and P5/7.p assume the 1° and 2° fates, respectively.
source: Cells P6.p and P5/7.p assume the 1° and 2° fates, respectively, and after three divisions form the vulva.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about wild-type C. elegans vulval development.

claim: P6.p and P5/7.p cells form the vulva after three divisions.
source: Cells P6.p and P5/7.p assume the 1° and 2° fates, respectively, and after three divisions form the vulva.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about C. elegans vulval development.

claim: P3/4.p and P8.p are assigned fate 3°.
source: The remaining cells, P3/4.p and P8.p, are assigned fate 3°.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about wild-type C. elegans vulval development.

claim: P3/4.p and P8.p divide once and fuse with the hypodermis.
source: They divide once and fuse with the hypodermis.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about the fate of 3° cells in C. elegans.

claim: The model represents each cell's state as traveling in a landscape with three valleys (fates) in two dimensions.
source: These basic facts suggested a model in which each cell travels in a landscape with three valleys (fates) that we represent in two dimensions to allow EGF and Notch to tilt the landscape independently as development proceeds (Corson and Siggia, 2012).
evidence: This describes the fundamental structure of the geometric model.

claim: The two-dimensional representation allows EGF and Notch to tilt the landscape independently as development proceeds.
source: These basic facts suggested a model in which each cell travels in a landscape with three valleys (fates) that we represent in two dimensions to allow EGF and Notch to tilt the landscape independently as development proceeds (Corson and Siggia, 2012).
evidence: This explains the rationale for the two-dimensional model structure.

claim: The movement of a cell in the landscape depends on parameters that quantify the influence of each signal on the direction of motion.
source: The movement of a cell in the landscape depends on parameters that quantify the influence of each signal on the direction of motion in the landscape.
evidence: This describes how signals affect cell dynamics in the model.

claim: Parameter values were obtained from known terminal VPC fate patterns of animals defective in the two signaling pathways.
source: Values for these parameters were obtained from known terminal VPC fate patterns of animals defective in the two signaling pathways, as well as from limited time-specific perturbations (ablation of the AC at different stages) (Greenwald et al., 1983; Ferguson and Horvitz, 1985; Sternberg, 1988; Sundaram and Greenwald, 1993; Koga and Ohshima, 1995; Simske et al., 1995; Shaye and Greenwald, 2002; Félix, 2007; Milloz et al., 2008; Komatsu et al., 2008; Hoyos et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the data sources used for parameter fitting, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Parameter values were obtained from time-specific perturbations including ablation of the AC at different stages.
source: Values for these parameters were obtained from known terminal VPC fate patterns of animals defective in the two signaling pathways, as well as from limited time-specific perturbations (ablation of the AC at different stages) (Greenwald et al., 1983; Ferguson and Horvitz, 1985; Sternberg, 1988; Sundaram and Greenwald, 1993; Koga and Ohshima, 1995; Simske et al., 1995; Shaye and Greenwald, 2002; Félix, 2007; Milloz et al., 2008; Komatsu et al., 2008; Hoyos et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the data sources used for parameter fitting, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Partially penetrant phenotypes are ideal for parameter fitting as they define the locations of ridges.
source: Partially penetrant phenotypes are ideal for parameter fitting as they define the locations of ridges.
evidence: This is a methodological claim about the value of partially penetrant phenotypes for model fitting.

claim: The model focuses on the competence period during vulval development.
source: From this data alone, focusing on the competence period (Ambros, 1999; Wang and Sternberg, 1999), we built a quantitative model for how EGF and Notch signals control fates, without considering the underlying complex genetic networks (Corson and Siggia, 2012).
evidence: This describes a key temporal constraint of the model, supported by citations.

claim: The model was built without considering the underlying complex genetic networks.
source: From this data alone, focusing on the competence period (Ambros, 1999; Wang and Sternberg, 1999), we built a quantitative model for how EGF and Notch signals control fates, without considering the underlying complex genetic networks (Corson and Siggia, 2012).
evidence: This describes a key feature of the modeling approach.

claim: The model has no fitting parameters that would couple the EGF and Notch pathways.
source: Our model has no fitting parameters that would couple the EGF and Notch pathways, implying that that if we fit two alleles, one in each pathway, then the outcome of the cross is defined with no additional freedom.
evidence: This is a key feature of the model structure that enables predictive power.

claim: If two alleles (one in each pathway) are fit, then the outcome of the cross is defined with no additional freedom.
source: Our model has no fitting parameters that would couple the EGF and Notch pathways, implying that that if we fit two alleles, one in each pathway, then the outcome of the cross is defined with no additional freedom.
evidence: This is a consequence of the model structure and demonstrates its predictive capability.

claim: The model is sufficient to explain experiments showing epistasis, including non-intuitive interactions previously attributed to context-dependent action of signals.
source: Still, the model is sufficient to explain experiments showing epistasis, including non-intuitive interactions that were previously attributed to a context-dependent action of the signals, for example low EGF can promote 2° fate acquisition, or biochemical interactions between the pathways in a single cell.
evidence: This claim is supported by the model's ability to explain experimental observations without invoking context-dependent signaling.

claim: Low EGF can promote 2° fate acquisition.
source: Still, the model is sufficient to explain experiments showing epistasis, including non-intuitive interactions that were previously attributed to a context-dependent action of the signals, for example low EGF can promote 2° fate acquisition, or biochemical interactions between the pathways in a single cell.
evidence: This is an example of a non-intuitive interaction that the model explains.

claim: The model can predict context-dependent signals since it applies a nonlinear function to a linear combination of the two vectors representing the pathways.
source: The model can predict context-dependent signals since it applies a nonlinear function to a linear combination of the two vectors representing the pathways.
evidence: This explains the mathematical mechanism by which the model produces context-dependent behavior without explicit coupling.

claim: Barkoulas et al. (2013) quantified EGF levels in a series of perturbation lines and examined cell fate outcomes in multiple combinations with Notch perturbation lines.
source: Recent work (Barkoulas et al., 2013) quantified EGF levels in a series of perturbation lines and examined the cell fate outcomes in multiple combinations with Notch perturbation lines.
evidence: This describes new experimental data used to refine and test the model.

claim: The new data from Barkoulas et al. (2013) allows further quantitative refinement of the model.
source: The new data allows further quantitative refinement of the model, and an extensive test of its predictions.
evidence: This describes how the new data was used to improve the model.

claim: The refined model generates a phase diagram that displays the terminal vulval cell fate pattern as a function of EGF and Notch signal strengths.
source: Using the refined model, we now generate a phase diagram that displays the terminal vulval cell fate pattern as a function of the EGF and Notch signal strengths.
evidence: This describes the main output of the refined model.

claim: The phase diagram predicts the existence of special transition points where epistasis is particularly evident.
source: The diagram predicts the existence of special transition points where epistasis is particularly evident.
evidence: This is a key prediction of the model based on the phase diagram structure.

claim: Special transition points organize the entire phase diagram and define allowed and forbidden phenotypic transitions in response to continuous changes in signal strength.
source: These special points organize the entire phase diagram and define allowed and forbidden phenotypic transitions in response to continuous changes in signal strength.
evidence: This describes the structural importance of triple points in the phase diagram.

claim: Verification of transition points is an important goal of future experiments.
source: Verification of these transition points is an important goal of future experiments.
evidence: This is a recommendation for future experimental work.

claim: Taking a more abstract, yet mathematically rigorous, geometric approach can reveal underlying principles of development.
source: Our data demonstrate that taking a more abstract, yet mathematically rigorous, geometric approach can reveal underlying principles of development, and can provide immediate quantitative predictions more difficult to obtain through kinetic modeling of the complex underlying gene and protein networks.
evidence: This is a general claim about the value of the geometric modeling approach.

claim: The geometric approach can provide immediate quantitative predictions more difficult to obtain through kinetic modeling of complex gene and protein networks.
source: Our data demonstrate that taking a more abstract, yet mathematically rigorous, geometric approach can reveal underlying principles of development, and can provide immediate quantitative predictions more difficult to obtain through kinetic modeling of the complex underlying gene and protein networks.
evidence: This is a comparative claim about the advantages of geometric modeling over detailed kinetic models.

claim: At the beginning of competence, all cells in an equivalence group start at the same position.
source: At the beginning of competence (t = 0+ signal reception on), all cells in an equivalence group start at the same position, but P6.p receives a strong EGF signal from the AC which makes 1° the only possible fate.
evidence: This describes the initial conditions in the model.

claim: P6.p receives a strong EGF signal from the AC which makes 1° the only possible fate.
source: At the beginning of competence (t = 0+ signal reception on), all cells in an equivalence group start at the same position, but P6.p receives a strong EGF signal from the AC which makes 1° the only possible fate.
evidence: This describes the effect of EGF signaling on P6.p in the model.

claim: At mid-competence, P6.p reaches the threshold for Notch ligand production and produces Notch ligands.
source: At mid-competence, P6.p reaches the dashed line and produces Notch ligands.
evidence: This describes a key event in the model dynamics.

claim: Notch ligand production by P6.p yields autocrine signaling in P6.p and paracrine signaling in P5/7.p.
source: This yields autocrine signaling in P6.p (green arrow) and paracrine signaling in P5/7.p that eliminates all fates except 2°.
evidence: This describes the effect of Notch ligand production in the model.

claim: Paracrine Notch signaling from P6.p to P5/7.p eliminates all fates except 2° in P5/7.p.
source: This yields autocrine signaling in P6.p (green arrow) and paracrine signaling in P5/7.p that eliminates all fates except 2°.
evidence: This describes the effect of lateral Notch signaling in the model.

claim: At the end of competence, the fate plane reverts to its configuration in the absence of signaling.
source: At the end of competence (t = 1+ signal reception off) the fate plane reverts to its configuration in the absence of signaling, which is virtually identical to that for P4/8.p at earlier times since it receives no signals under WT conditions.
evidence: This describes the model behavior after the competence period ends.

claim: Induced cells find themselves in specific fate domains and progress toward the corresponding terminal fates after competence ends.
source: However, the induced cells find themselves in the red or green regions and progress toward the 1° or 2° fates.
evidence: This describes how cells become committed to their fates in the model.

claim: Under wild-type conditions, each cloud of cell states is well inside a single territory, corresponding to an invariant fate pattern.
source: Under the WT conditions shown here, each cloud is well inside a single territory, corresponding to an invariant fate pattern.
evidence: This describes the robustness of wild-type development in the model.

claim: The model assumes fixed EGF levels that are constant in time, consistent with observed mRNA levels in the AC.
source: The VPCs receive graded EGF levels that are constant in time, consistent with observed mRNA levels in the AC (Barkoulas et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes a key assumption of the model, supported by experimental data.

claim: Notch ligand production is turned on in cells approaching the 1° fate.
source: Notch ligand production, on the other hand, is turned on in cells approaching the 1° fate (see the response in P7.p at t = 0.5 after P6.p has reached the dotted line in Figure 1D).
evidence: This describes a key feature of Notch signaling dynamics in the model.

claim: The model incorporates fluctuations to account for partially penetrant phenotypes.
source: The model also incorporates fluctuations to account for partially penetrant phenotypes.
evidence: This describes how the model accounts for variability in experimental outcomes.

claim: Animals heterozygous for null mutations in lin-3 or lin-12 are described in the model by dividing the signal by two.
source: Animals heterozygous for null mutations in lin-3 or lin-12 are described in the model by dividing the signal by two ('half dose').
evidence: This describes how heterozygous mutations are modeled.

claim: The EGF level for the JU1107 overexpression line was set according to the measured lin-3 mRNA level.
source: The EGF level for one overexpression line (JU1107) was set according to the measured lin-3 mRNA level.
evidence: This describes how EGF levels were determined for one experimental line.

claim: For other perturbations, the change in signal is included as a fitting parameter.
source: For other perturbations, the change in signal is included as a fitting parameter, cf. Table S2.
evidence: This describes the approach for modeling perturbations without measured signal levels.

claim: Notch null mutations result in the formation of two anchor cells.
source: * Notch null mutations result in the formation of two anchor cells, thus the effect of suppressing Notch signaling between VPCs it not obvious; however, several lines of evidence suggest that it yields the pattern 33133.
evidence: This is a known biological fact about Notch null mutations.

claim: Several lines of evidence suggest that suppressing Notch signaling between VPCs yields the pattern 33133.
source: * Notch null mutations result in the formation of two anchor cells, thus the effect of suppressing Notch signaling between VPCs it not obvious; however, several lines of evidence suggest that it yields the pattern 33133.
evidence: This is based on interpretation of experimental evidence despite the complication of two anchor cells.

claim: let-23 mosaic animals (with no EGF receptors in P5/7.p) show wild-type fate patterns.
source: let-23 mosaic (no EGF receptors in P5/7 .p) wild type (Koga and Ohshima, 1995; Simske et al., 1995)
evidence: This is experimental data used to fit the model, supported by citations.

claim: Half dose of EGF (lin-3/+) results in wild-type fate patterns.
source: Half dose of EGF (lin-3/+) wild type (Ferguson and Horvitz, 1985)
evidence: This is experimental data showing that EGF is not limiting in wild-type, supported by citation.

claim: Half dose of Notch (lin-12/+) results in wild-type fate patterns.
source: Half dose of Notch (lin-12/+) wild type (Greenwald et al., 1983)
evidence: This is experimental data showing that Notch is not limiting in wild-type, supported by citation.

claim: No Notch signaling results in the fate pattern 33133.
source: No Notch signaling * 3° 3° 1° 3° 3° (Sundaram and Greenwald, 1993; Shaye and Greenwald, 2002; Komatsu et al., 2008)
evidence: This is experimental data used to fit the model, supported by citations.

claim: Notch null mutant with 2 ACs results in the fate pattern 31113.
source: Notch null mutant, 2 ACs * (described as 2 × WT EGF) 3° 1° 1° 1° 3° (Greenwald et al., 1983)
evidence: This is experimental data used to fit the model, supported by citation.

claim: lin-15 mutant (ectopic EGF) results in alternating 1° and 2° fates with or without AC.
source: lin-15 mutant (ectopic EGF; fit to ~0.4 × WT) alternating 1° and 2° fates (with or without AC) (Sternberg, 1988)
evidence: This is experimental data used to fit the model, supported by citation.

claim: The phase diagram has a Y-like shape at triple points reflecting the geometry of the fate plane.
source: The Y-like shape of the triple points reflects the geometry of the fate plane (Figure 1E), and the 45° slope of the boundary between 31113 and WT (green line to the right of T1) is a direct consequence of how the signals are combined in the model (linearly).
evidence: This explains the geometric origin of features in the phase diagram.

claim: The 45° slope of the boundary between 31113 and WT is a direct consequence of how the signals are combined in the model (linearly).
source: The Y-like shape of the triple points reflects the geometry of the fate plane (Figure 1E), and the 45° slope of the boundary between 31113 and WT (green line to the right of T1) is a direct consequence of how the signals are combined in the model (linearly).
evidence: This explains a specific feature of the phase diagram based on the model structure.

claim: The assumption of an exponential EGF gradient yields evenly spaced boundaries under low Notch.
source: Our assumption of an exponential EGF gradient yields evenly spaced boundaries under low Notch.
evidence: This explains a feature of the phase diagram based on a model assumption.

claim: The model correctly predicts the outcome of the JU2113 line (1.25 × WT EGF with reduced Notch).
source: This prediction is born out by experiment (Barkoulas et al., 2013). Whereas animals subjected to RNAi against lin-12/Notch (fit as 0.4 × WT Notch) show occasional conversion of P5/7.p to the 3° fate, elevating EGF to only 1.25 × WT results in a substantial fraction of P5/7.p cells adopting a 1° fate, Figure 3B–C and Table 4.
evidence: This is a comparison of model predictions with experimental data.

claim: The model predicts that in the lin-12 RNAi background, removing one EGF copy (50% EGF activity) would result in substantial conversion of P5/7.p to the 3° fates.
source: We predict that in the same RNAi background, removing one EGF copy (50% EGF activity) would result in substantial conversion of P5/7.p to the 3° fates.
evidence: This is a testable prediction of the model.

claim: EGF and Notch function independently in the model.
source: However, our model allows an apparently simpler explanation: EGF and Notch function independently, and because the path P1 cuts through a corner of the WT domain, changes up or down in EGF can result in conversion of 2° to 1° or 3° fates.
evidence: This is a key claim about the model structure that explains apparent epistasis.

claim: The strain JU2092 combines modest ectopic Notch activity with a defined level of EGF overexpression.
source: The strain JU2092 (Figure 4B,C2, Table 4) combines modest ectopic Notch activity (whose level we fit from an independent experiment, Figure 2C), with a defined level of EGF overexpression.
evidence: This describes the genetic background of an experimental line.

claim: In JU2092 animals, P4/8.p cells are partially converted to the 2° fate while leaving P5-7.p unaffected.
source: In these animals, P4/8.p cells are partially converted to the 2° fate while leaving P5-7.p unaffected.
evidence: This is an experimental observation that the model explains.

claim: When EGF levels are sufficiently large, P5/7.p transit through the 1° fate domain on their way to the 2° fate.
source: When EGF levels are sufficiently large, we predict that P5/7.p transit through the 1° fate domain on their way to the 2° fate, and thus transiently signal to P4/8.p.
evidence: This is a model prediction that explains the JU2092 phenotype.

claim: Transient signaling from P5/7.p synergizes with ectopic Notch activity to induce 2° fates in P4/8.p.
source: This transient signal synergizes with ectopic Notch activity to induce 2° fates in P4/8.p.
evidence: This is a model prediction that explains the JU2092 phenotype.

claim: The position of the line for Notch signaling threshold is required to explain the outcome of AC ablation experiments.
source: The same position of the line for Notch signaling is independently required to explain the outcome of AC ablation experiments (Corson and Siggia, 2012).
evidence: This shows that a model parameter is constrained by multiple independent experiments.

claim: Ectopic Notch activity favors the 1° fate in an EGF hypomorph.
source: Yet another observation affirming a context-dependent association of signals and fates is the observation that ectopic Notch activity favors the 1° fate in an EGF hypomorph (Barkoulas et al., 2013) (path P3 in Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation that appears counterintuitive but is explained by the model.

claim: The EGF hypomorph leaves P6.p poised between fates 3° and 1°.
source: The EGF hypomorph leaves P6.p poised between fates 3° and 1° and stretched out along the line connecting the saddle or decision point to the associated fates.
evidence: This describes the model state for P6.p in the EGF hypomorph background.

claim: The Notch signal is not parallel to the ridge leading into the saddle and favors fate 1°.
source: But the Notch signal has no reason to be parallel to the 'ridge' leading into the saddle and it in fact favors fate 1°, explaining the increased 1° fates with ectopic Notch.
evidence: This explains the counterintuitive effect of Notch in the EGF hypomorph based on the geometry of the fate plane.

claim: As a function of increasing Notch, the model predicts a peak in the fraction of 1° fated P6.p followed by their conversion to entirely 2° fates for highest Notch.
source: More generally as a function of increasing Notch, we predict a peak in the fraction of 1° fated P6.p followed by their conversion to entirely 2° fates for highest Notch as observed (Barkoulas et al., 2013), Figure 5B.
evidence: This is a model prediction that matches experimental observations.

claim: Mild EGF signaling can induce the 2° fate in a sensitized background of weak ectopic Notch.
source: A converse experiment (Zand et al., 2011) found that mild EGF signaling could induce the 2° fate in a sensitized background of weak ectopic Notch that alone was not strong enough to induce appreciable 2° fates.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from Zand et al., 2011.

claim: The sensitized state in the Zand et al. experiment is poised near the saddle point between fates 2° and 3°.
source: The fate plane of the model, Figure 5D, shows that the sensitized state is poised near the saddle point between fates 2° and 3°.
evidence: This is a model interpretation of the Zand et al. experiment.

claim: EGF can tip the balance and favor 2° fates because the EGF vector is not parallel to the flow into the decision point.
source: Again because the vector representing EGF is not parallel to the flow into the decision point, EGF can tip the balance and favors 2°.
evidence: This explains the synergy between EGF and Notch based on the geometry of the fate plane.

claim: The model can explain the enhanced fraction of 2° fates induced by EGF observed in Zand et al. (2011) from the flow in the fate plane around the saddle point, with no special assumptions.
source: We could explain the enhanced fraction of 2° fates induced by EGF observed in Zand et al. (2011), merely from the flow in the fate plane around the saddle point, with no special assumptions.
evidence: This contrasts the model's explanation with alternative interpretations.

claim: Zand et al. (2011) related the outcome to a switch between different Ras effectors, suggesting that the EGF vector rotated and pointed toward 2° for low ligand levels.
source: By contrast, Ref. (Zand et al., 2011) related this outcome to a switch between different Ras effectors, suggesting (if we translate to our language) that the EGF vector, whose direction remains fixed in our model, rotated and pointed upward toward 2° and away from 1° for low ligand levels.
evidence: This describes an alternative interpretation from the literature that the model does not require.

claim: Time-dependent perturbations during the competence period are more informative for model fitting and validation than end point data.
source: Time-dependent perturbations during the competence period, as exemplified by anchor cell ablation (Félix, 2007; Milloz et al., 2008), are more informative for model fitting and validation than end point data.
evidence: This is a methodological claim about the value of dynamic data.

claim: The model predicts that a Notch pulse early in induction diverts P6.p further away from the ridge between 3° and 1° than a late one, and thus induces more P6.p cells to the 1° fate.
source: A Notch pulse early in induction diverts P6.p further away from the ridge between 3° and 1° than a late one, and thus induces more P6.p cells to the 1° fate.
evidence: This is a model prediction about the timing-dependent effects of Notch perturbations.

claim: The model predicts dramatic effects if an early EGF pulse is applied in the lin-15(ts) background including P3.p.
source: Finally, we predict dramatic effects in the pure lin-15(ts) background, if we include P3.p in the model and then extend the duration of the heat pulse, Figure 6—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is a model prediction for a specific experimental perturbation.

claim: Because the induced EGF is uniform across the VPCs, P3.p gets induced and provides an additional lateral signal to P4.p.
source: Because the induced EGF is uniform across the VPCs, P3.p gets induced and provides an additional lateral signal to P4.p.
evidence: This explains the predicted asymmetry between P4.p and P8.p.

claim: There is a marked asymmetry between P4/8.p in the degree to which they are induced to 2° fates in the lin-15(ts) background with extended heat pulse.
source: Thus, there is a marked asymmetry between P4/8.p in the degree to which they are induced to 2° fates.
evidence: This is a model prediction.

claim: The predicted 22123 pattern is noteworthy since it is induced by EGF and involves adjacent 2° fates.
source: To realize this state may require some tuning of the intensity of the temperature step, but the predicted 22123 pattern is noteworthy since it is induced by EGF and involves adjacent 2° fates.
evidence: This highlights the counterintuitive nature of the prediction.

claim: The model fits imply that the EGF pathway is saturated in P6.p under WT levels.
source: Our fits imply that the EGF pathway is saturated in P6.p under WT levels.
evidence: This is an inference from the fitted parameter values.

claim: EGF activity and the rate at which P6.p progresses toward the 1° fate should not be too sensitive to moderate changes in EGF dosage.
source: As a result, EGF activity and the rate at which P6.p progresses toward the 1° fate should not be too sensitive to moderate changes in EGF dosage.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the saturation of the EGF pathway.

claim: The prediction of EGF saturation is consistent with the observed dynamics of Notch ligand expression in P6.p under EGF overexpression, which is similar to WT.
source: This prediction is consistent with the observed dynamics of Notch ligand expression in P6.p (an indicator of EGF activity and/or progression toward the 1° fate) under EGF overexpression, which is similar to WT (van Zon et al., 2015).
evidence: This compares a model prediction with experimental observations.

claim: The saturation of the EGF pathway can be tested by ablating the anchor cell in an EGF +/- background.
source: The saturation of the EGF pathway can be tested by ablating the anchor cell in an EGF +/- background.
evidence: This is a suggested experimental test of a model prediction.

claim: The model predicts little change from WT for AC ablation in an EGF +/- background, in contrast with predictions for ablations in Notch perturbation lines.
source: We predict little change from the outcome for WT animals, in contrast with predictions for ablations in Notch perturbation lines (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a specific testable prediction of the model.

claim: It is well known that Notch signaling inhibits the MAPK pathway and Ras activation inhibits Notch signaling.
source: However, it is well known that Notch signaling inhibits the MAPK pathway and Ras activation inhibits Notch signaling (Shaye and Greenwald, 2002; Berset et al., 2001; Yoo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge about pathway interactions, supported by citations.

claim: A simple way to incorporate pathway coupling is to down-regulate Notch signaling in 1° fated cells along the same threshold that defines the production of Notch ligands.
source: A simple way to incorporate one such coupling in the model, with no additional parameters, is to down-regulate Notch signaling in 1° fated cells along the same threshold that defines the production of Notch ligands, cf. (Shaye and Greenwald, 2002).
evidence: This describes a model modification to incorporate pathway coupling.

claim: Fitting the modified model with pathway coupling to the same data results in only minor adjustments to parameter values.
source: Fitting this modified model to the same data, we find only minor adjustments to parameter values (Table 2), and the predictions are largely unchanged.
evidence: This shows that the main model results are robust to the inclusion of pathway coupling.

claim: The phase diagram with pathway coupling is very similar to the main model, with the most noticeable difference in the regime of reduced Notch and excess EGF.
source: The resulting phase diagram, Figure 7B, is very similar to Figure 2A. The most noticeable difference is in the regime of reduced Notch and excess EGF: the 21112 domain extends to lower EGF levels, forming a longer boundary with the WT domain.
evidence: This compares the phase diagrams of the two model versions.

claim: Down-regulation of Notch in 1° fated cells restores a saddle point on the 1°−2° boundary that partitions the cells into distinct 1° and 2° groups.
source: Down-regulation of Notch in 1° fated cells restores a saddle point on the 1°−2° boundary that partitions the cells into distinct 1° and 2° groups, allowing the 1° cells to signal strongly to their neighbors.
evidence: This explains the effect of pathway coupling on cell fate correlations.

claim: The correlation between 1° fates in P5/7.p and 2° fates in P4/8.p is consistent with observations in the JU2113 line.
source: The resulting correlation between 1° fates in P5/7.p and 2° fates in P4/8.p is consistent with observations in the JU2113 line, with a slightly lower measured EGF level (1.25 × WT).
evidence: This compares the model with pathway coupling to experimental data.

claim: The bistability in P5/7.p implies a direct transition from a WT pattern to 21112.
source: The same bistability in P5/7.p implies a direct transition from a WT pattern to 21112, which is a strong prediction of our geometric modeling scheme, Figure 7B.
evidence: This is a prediction of the model with pathway coupling.

claim: A proliferating pool of progenitor cells that can be diverted into two mutually exclusive states by different signals is common in development.
source: It is common in development to find a proliferating pool of progenitor cells that can be diverted into two mutually exclusive states by different signals.
evidence: This is a general statement about developmental biology.

claim: The split of pluripotent epiblast cells into mesendoderm or neural fates at gastrulation is an example of two signals regulating cell fate.
source: An example from early mammalian development is the split of the pluripotent epiblast cells into mesendoderm or neural fates at the time of gastrulation.
evidence: This provides an example of a developmental system with similar logic to vulval development.

claim: The fate plane model with three possible fates is generic.
source: Thus, our fate plane model with three possible fates is generic.
evidence: This claims that the modeling approach is broadly applicable.

claim: The modeling proceeds from general mathematical embodiment of basic principles of development: cell fates are discrete, cells are competent to respond to signals over a limited period, and cells are committed when they assume their normal fates without additional signals.
source: The modeling proceeds from a general mathematical embodiment of the basic principles of development: cell fates are discrete, cells are competent to respond to signals over a limited period, and cells are committed when they assume their normal fates without additional signals.
evidence: This describes the fundamental assumptions underlying the modeling approach.

claim: Fates in the model are very schematic and say nothing about the gene networks or morphogenetic events that ultimately define the fates.
source: 'Fates' in the model are very schematic, they say nothing about the gene networks or morphogenetic events that ultimately define the fates.
evidence: This clarifies the level of abstraction in the model.

claim: This simplification is plausible if the competence period ends before overt fate specification or differentiation occurs.
source: This simplification is plausible if the competence period ends before overt fate specification or differentiation occurs.
evidence: This justifies the abstraction of fates in the model.

claim: Vulval patterning in C. elegans conforms to the assumptions of the model.
source: Vulval patterning in C. elegans conforms to our assumptions (Ambros, 1999; Wang and Sternberg, 1999), and adds the simplification that the fates are terminal, so we can ignore subsequent bifurcations of the Waddington valleys.
evidence: This justifies the application of the modeling approach to vulval development.

claim: The fate plane represents the state of a cell.
source: Our fate plane represents the state of a cell.
evidence: This defines what the fate plane represents in the model.

claim: The motion of a cell in the plane depends on signals impinging on that cell at the moment in question.
source: The motion of a cell in the plane will depend on signals impinging on that cell at the moment in question.
evidence: This describes how signals affect cell dynamics in the model.

claim: The production of Notch ligand depends only on where the cell is, not on the signals.
source: Logically, the production of Notch ligand will depend only on where the cell is, not on the signals.
evidence: This describes a key feature of how Notch signaling is modeled.

claim: The onset of Notch ligand production is parameterized by a line in the fate plane.
source: Thus, we parameterized the onset of Notch ligand production by a line in the fate plane.
evidence: This describes how Notch ligand production is represented in the model.

claim: The geometry that accompanies the Waddington landscapes informs the interpretation of genetic experiments.
source: The geometry that accompanies the Waddington landscapes informs the interpretation of genetic experiments.
evidence: This is a general claim about the value of the geometric approach.

claim: Since the model has three distinct states represented as valleys, there must be ridges between adjacent fates.
source: Since the model has three distinct states represented as valleys, there must be ridges between adjacent fates, with the property that with a little noise half the cells will go to each state.
evidence: This is a mathematical consequence of the model structure.

claim: The saddle point is the low point on a ridge between two fates.
source: The aptly named saddle point is the low point on such a ridge.
evidence: This defines the saddle point in the context of the model.

claim: For cells positioned anywhere near the ridge that feeds into the saddle, a small initial perturbation can lead to large changes in outcomes that are generally impossible to predict without a model.
source: The topographic analogy makes it very evident that for cells positioned anywhere near the ridge that feeds into the saddle, a small initial perturbation can lead to large changes in outcomes that are generally impossible to predict without a model.
evidence: This explains the importance of the geometric representation for understanding cell fate decisions.

claim: A 'sensitized background' in genetics is precisely an allele that flows near a saddle point.
source: A 'sensitized background' in genetics is precisely an allele that flows near a saddle point.
evidence: This connects genetic terminology to the geometric model.

claim: To infer the activity of a gene by crossing it into a sensitized background may require a model.
source: Thus to infer the activity of a gene by crossing it into a sensitized background may require a model, and conversely such experiments are very informative for model fitting since they expose the boundaries between fates.
evidence: This is a methodological claim about the interpretation of genetic experiments.

claim: Experiments in sensitized backgrounds are very informative for model fitting since they expose the boundaries between fates.
source: Thus to infer the activity of a gene by crossing it into a sensitized background may require a model, and conversely such experiments are very informative for model fitting since they expose the boundaries between fates.
evidence: This is a methodological claim about the value of certain types of experiments.

claim: The modeling approach yields the most parsimonious parameterization of how two signals can control three fates.
source: Our modeling approach yields the most parsimonious parameterization of how two signals can control three fates.
evidence: This is a claim about the efficiency of the modeling approach.

claim: The flow diagram is two dimensional to accommodate the two signals.
source: The flow diagram is two dimensional to accommodate the two signals, there are three fixed points, one for each fate, and then mathematics requires the presence of two saddles.
evidence: This explains the mathematical structure of the model.

claim: Mathematics requires the presence of two saddles in the model.
source: The flow diagram is two dimensional to accommodate the two signals, there are three fixed points, one for each fate, and then mathematics requires the presence of two saddles.
evidence: This is a mathematical constraint on the model structure.

claim: The 12 parameters in the model all plausibly can be independently varied.
source: It is informative to scan the list of 12 parameters in Table 2 that appear in the model. They all plausibly can be independently varied, for example, the time scale, noise level, EGF gradient, and autocrine signal all describe different phenomena.
evidence: This justifies the number of parameters in the model.

claim: Other models for vulva have yet more parameters than the geometric model.
source: The other models for vulva we discuss below have yet more parameters.
evidence: This compares the parsimony of the geometric model to other approaches.

claim: Fisher et al. (2007) constructed a discrete model for the vulva system incorporating virtually all relevant genes.
source: Reference (Fisher et al., 2007) constructs a discrete model for the vulva system incorporating virtually all relevant genes.
evidence: This describes an alternative modeling approach from the literature.

claim: The Fisher et al. (2007) model was shown to be consistent by logical programming techniques.
source: It was shown to be consistent by logical programming techniques.
evidence: This describes a feature of the Fisher et al. model.

claim: The Fisher et al. (2007) model does not deal with partial penetrance or treat continuously variable morphogens.
source: However, from our perspective it does not deal with partial penetrance or treat continuously variable morphogens.
evidence: This identifies limitations of the Fisher et al. model compared to the geometric approach.

claim: Hoyos et al. (2011) implemented a differential equation model built from selected genes with Michaelis-Menten dynamics that required over 40 parameters.
source: A differential equation built from selected genes with Michaelis-Menten dynamics was implemented in Hoyos et al., (2011) and required over 40 parameters.
evidence: This describes another alternative modeling approach and its complexity.

claim: Giurumescu et al. (2009) describe a cell with two coordinates (for Notch and EGF).
source: Closest to our approach is Reference (Giurumescu et al., 2009), who describe a cell with two coordinates (for Notch and EGF).
evidence: This describes a modeling approach similar to the geometric model.

claim: Giurumescu et al. (2009) do not fit partial penetrance data, or autocrine signaling, ignore the anchor cell ablation data, and do not build in multistability.
source: They also do not fit partial penetrance data, or autocrine signaling, ignore the anchor cell ablation data that we found crucial for model selection, and also do not build in multistability.
evidence: This identifies differences between the Giurumescu et al. model and the geometric model.

claim: Giurumescu et al. (2009) use 13 dimensionful parameters, one more than the geometric model.
source: Nevertheless they use 13 dimensionful parameters, one more than we do.
evidence: This compares the number of parameters in the two models.

claim: The Notch and EGF signals are described as two vectors combined by vector addition in the model.
source: We were able to describe the Notch and EGF signals as two vectors combined by vector addition since they appear inside of nonlinear functions that build in the basic landscape of the VPC dynamics, namely three fixed points and two saddles (Methods).
evidence: This describes the mathematical structure of how signals are combined in the model.

claim: What appeared as interactions when counting VPC fates disappear when fit to the geometric model.
source: This is why we assert that the inference of interactions is contingent on how we chose to represent the data, and the bulk of this paper is devoted to showing that what appeared as interactions when counting VPC fates, disappear when fit to our model as shown in Figure 3–5.
evidence: This is a key claim about how the model reinterprets apparent pathway interactions.

claim: Multiple steps in a signaling pathway are collapsed into one parameter in the model.
source: Multiple steps in a signaling pathway are collapsed into one parameter; nevertheless, the model can capture intra-pathway interactions.
evidence: This describes the level of abstraction in the model.

claim: The model can capture intra-pathway interactions despite collapsing multiple steps into one parameter.
source: Multiple steps in a signaling pathway are collapsed into one parameter; nevertheless, the model can capture intra-pathway interactions.
evidence: This claims that the model can represent certain types of complexity despite its abstraction.

claim: The model described the cross between a loss-of-function mutant in the MAPK phosphatase LIP-1 and ectopic EGF from lin-15 by first adding the lin-15 contribution to the EGF from the anchor cell and then multiplying the sum by a parameter larger than one.
source: In (Corson and Siggia, 2012), we described the cross between a loss-of-function mutant in the MAPK phosphatase, LIP-1 and ectopic EGF from lin-15, by first adding the lin-15 contribution to the EGF from the anchor cell and then multiplying the sum by a parameter larger than one to account for loss of the phosphatase.
evidence: This describes how a specific genetic interaction was modeled.

claim: The model fits the genetic data in Berset et al. (2001) even though LIP-1 is a Notch target and biochemically inhibits EGF signaling.
source: Our model that takes a linear combination of the vectors parameterizing each pathway and passes the vector sum through a nonlinear function, fits the genetic data in (Berset et al., 2001) even though LIP-1 is a Notch target and biochemically inhibits EGF signaling.
evidence: This shows that the model can explain genetic data without explicitly representing biochemical interactions.

claim: The model does not need to introduce a new fitting parameter for the down regulation of the MAPK cascade by the LIP-1 phosphatase to explain the genetic data.
source: We do not have to introduce a new fitting parameter for the down regulation of the MAPK cascade by the LIP-1 phosphatase to explain the genetic data.
evidence: This demonstrates the parsimony of the model.

claim: In the absence of fitting parameters explicitly coupling the two pathways, the model has reproduced effects previously attributed to pathway epistasis simply by including the basic genetic facts of vulval patterning.
source: In the absence of fitting parameters explicitly coupling the two pathways, our model has reproduced effects previously attributed to pathway epistasis simply by including the basic genetic facts of vulval patterning.
evidence: This is a key claim about the model's ability to explain epistasis without explicit coupling parameters.

claim: The most visible manifestations of intrinsic pathway interactions are correlations between the fates of adjacent cells.
source: The most visible manifestations of intrinsic pathway interactions we found are correlations between the fates of adjacent cells.
evidence: This identifies a specific type of phenomenon that requires pathway coupling in the model.

claim: Mutual pathway inhibition builds determination into the model.
source: Mutual pathway inhibition builds determination into our model, that is, a cell that gets close enough to its terminal state cannot be deflected from that state by ectopic signals.
evidence: This explains a consequence of including pathway coupling in the model.

claim: Separate parameters would be needed for the down regulation of Notch by EGF and the inhibition of MAPK by Notch signaling to go further with pathway coupling.
source: To go further, separate parameters would be needed for the down regulation of Notch by EGF and the inhibition of MAPK by Notch signaling (Shaye and Greenwald, 2002; Berset et al., 2001; Yoo et al., 2004), which we have not pursued since the necessary data are still very sparse, and this would have obscured effects that are independent of pathway interactions.
evidence: This explains why more detailed pathway coupling was not pursued.

claim: The most informative experiments to fit a dynamic model manipulate signaling during the competence period when the cell is poised among its fates.
source: Intuitively, the most informative experiments to fit a dynamic model manipulate signaling during the competence period when the cell is poised among its fates.
evidence: This is a methodological claim about experimental design.

claim: The timed anchor cell ablations were very instructive for the vulva model.
source: The timed anchor cell ablations were very instructive for the vulva model.
evidence: This is a claim about the value of specific experiments for model development.

claim: With recent advances in microfluidics, one can follow larval development for up to three days and image the worms every 8 min.
source: With recent advances in microfluidics (Keil et al., 2017) one can follow larval development for up to three days and image the worms every 8 min.
evidence: This describes new experimental capabilities relevant to testing the model.

claim: All the vulva divisions can be scored with DIC optics.
source: All the vulva divisions can be scored with DIC optics, and it is possible to control signals with temperature and ts-signaling alleles.
evidence: This describes experimental capabilities for testing the model.

claim: It is possible to control signals with temperature and ts-signaling alleles in microfluidic devices.
source: All the vulva divisions can be scored with DIC optics, and it is possible to control signals with temperature and ts-signaling alleles.
evidence: This describes experimental capabilities for testing the model.

claim: The phase diagram forces the recognition that individual phases have boundaries and that boundaries will in general meet at triple points.
source: A phase diagram forces the recognition that individual phases have boundaries and that boundaries will in general meet at triple points.
evidence: This is a general claim about the value of phase diagrams for understanding developmental systems.

claim: A model will assign coordinates to features in the phase diagram and allow experiments to be targeted to interesting points.
source: A model will assign coordinates to all these features and allow experiments to be targeted to interesting points.
evidence: This is a claim about the practical value of the modeling approach.

claim: Independent of a specific model, consideration of geometry unifies seemingly disparate outcomes.
source: Independent of a specific model, consideration of geometry unifies seemingly disparate outcomes.
evidence: This is a general claim about the value of geometric thinking in developmental biology.

claim: Models that define the fate plane geometrically and then fit to genes can unify what appear to be different signaling modalities.
source: Models that define the fate plane geometrically and then fit to genes can unify what appear to be different signaling modalities.
evidence: This is a general claim about the power of the geometric modeling approach.

claim: The relative importance of induction of 2° vs. 'lateral inhibition' of 1° by Notch has been debated.
source: The relative importance of induction of 2° vs. 'lateral inhibition' of 1° (Sternberg, 1988) by Notch has been debated.
evidence: This describes a debate in the literature about Notch function.

claim: Once we insist fates 1° and 2° are distinct (bistability), there is no distinction between favoring one or inhibiting the other.
source: While biochemically the distinction may be very clear (e.g. when Notch signaling deactivates the MAPK pathway [Berset et al., 2001; Yoo et al., 2004]), once we insist fates 1° and 2° are distinct (bistability) there is no distinction between favoring one or inhibiting the other.
evidence: This is a conceptual claim about how bistability affects the interpretation of signaling.

claim: The extensive data in Barkoulas et al. (2013) requires the authors to admit context-dependent signals.
source: While the extensive data in (Barkoulas et al., 2013) requires the authors to admit context-dependent signals (e.g. lateral inhibition vs. induction depends on EGF), our model accounts for all contexts with one set of parameters.
evidence: This contrasts the interpretation in Barkoulas et al. with the geometric model's interpretation.

claim: The geometric model accounts for all contexts with one set of parameters.
source: While the extensive data in (Barkoulas et al., 2013) requires the authors to admit context-dependent signals (e.g. lateral inhibition vs. induction depends on EGF), our model accounts for all contexts with one set of parameters.
evidence: This is a key claim about the parsimony and explanatory power of the geometric model.

claim: Vulval patterning is often conceptualized as an interplay of 'graded' (EGF level defines 1° vs. 2° fates) and 'sequential' (Notch induces 2° fates) signaling.
source: Similarly, vulval patterning is often conceptualized as an interplay of 'graded' (EGF level defines 1° vs. 2° fates [Katz et al., 1995; Sternberg and Horvitz, 1986]) and 'sequential' (Notch induces 2° fates [Koga and Ohshima, 1995; Simske et al., 1995]) signaling, which are proposed to be partially redundant (Kenyon, 1995).
evidence: This describes a conceptual framework from the literature.

claim: The quantitative model suggests a specific instance of partial redundancy: EGF reaching P5/7.p is not required for 2° fate induction but reduces loss of 2° fates under reduced Notch activity.
source: Our quantitative model suggests a specific instance of this: EGF reaching P5/7.p is not required for 2° fate induction but reduces loss of 2° fates under reduced Notch activity (Corson and Siggia, 2012).
evidence: This is a specific prediction of the model about the relationship between EGF and Notch.

claim: Genes and their interactions are the ultimate building blocks of development.
source: Genes and their interactions are the ultimate building blocks of development, so how can a phenomenological model that eschews any one to one correspondence with genes contribute to our knowledge of development?
evidence: This acknowledges the fundamental role of genes while questioning the necessity of gene-level models.

claim: For any signaling pathway, there are upwards of five components required from receptor to transcription and already 10's of parameters.
source: For any signaling pathway, there are upwards of five components required from receptor to transcription and already 10's of parameters.
evidence: This describes the complexity of detailed pathway models.

claim: There are solid grounds for believing most parameters in detailed pathway models do not matter for the behavior of the system.
source: There are solid grounds for believing most of these parameters do not matter for the behavior of the system (http://www.lassp.cornell.edu/sethna/Sloppy/).
evidence: This cites work on 'sloppy' models to justify parameter reduction.

claim: It is far from evident that actual parameters fit to cell culture systems have any relevance to the embryo.
source: Though pathway components and their biochemical properties have been elucidated in cell culture systems, it is far from evident that actual parameters fit to those systems have any relevance to the embryo.
evidence: This questions the transferability of parameters from in vitro to in vivo systems.

claim: If the goal is to be more quantitative about how an egg turns into an embryo, it is not clear how denser lists of genes and their interactions will help.
source: If the goal is to be more quantitative about how an egg turns into an embryo, then it is not clear to us, how denser lists of genes and their interactions will help.
evidence: This questions the value of comprehensive gene-level models for understanding development.

claim: Pieces of the developmental problem will be parameterized and the components joined in a structure defined by phenomenology.
source: Rather pieces of the problem will be parameterized and the components joined in a structure defined by phenomenology.
evidence: This proposes an alternative modeling strategy based on phenomenology.

claim: Evolution has built many levels of redundancy into development that insure a robust outcome but complicate efforts to reconstruct the process from its genetic components.
source: Evolution has built many levels of redundancy into development that insure a robust outcome but complicate efforts to reconstruct the process from its genetic components.
evidence: This is a general claim about the challenges of understanding development from genes.

claim: Geometric models take a step back from genetic reductionism and impose basic embryological phenomenology.
source: Geometric models take a step back from genetic reductionism and impose basic embryological phenomenology (competence, commitment, determination etc.).
evidence: This describes the philosophical approach of geometric modeling.

claim: Geometric models begin from a parsimonious representation of how signals define fates that largely eliminates redundancy among parameters.
source: They begin from a parsimonious representation of how signals define fates that largely eliminates redundancy among parameters, and leads to sharper fits and more believable predictions.
evidence: This is a claim about the advantages of the geometric modeling approach.

claim: Geometric models should be the method of choice when confronted with sparse in-vivo data in developmental biology.
source: Geometric models should be the method of choice when confronted with sparse in-vivo data in developmental biology (Corson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a recommendation for when to use geometric modeling approaches.
